question: For the historical requirements relevant to the current client task, reconstruct their last valid state immediately before the current task. Do not apply the current task to that state.

target_task.speaker: client
target_task.text: The script already specified the shot angles I wanted and explicitly noted that the storyboard angles were wrong. If you followed only the storyboard reel rather than the script, that explains why we misunderstood each other. Since I can’t reliably create images with the right angles to demonstrate them in the reel, what alternative process would work for you? How should I communicate each angle so you can render the shot correctly?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The new contract is for $850, with milestones organized by scene. I’ve also uploaded a revised script to the shared google folder; it has only a few small changes from the previous version. Since you don’t need to create the text cards, I’ll handle those myself. That may leave a little extra in funds for fine-tuning, although we’ll have to see how things go. Please let me know if anything is unclear. Thanks!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: If any questions come up while I read through the script again, I’ll write to you.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Ok great

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Ppl

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Because the artistic style can gradually drift, please do everything possible to keep it consistent and get the intended look exactly right.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Before I proceed with the remaining work, I’ll generate an image and send it to you for approval.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’m currently analyzing the SQ4 storyboard images. Should the video use color images or black-and-white ones?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For the video format, which orientation should I use: vertical or horizontal?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: To reduce costs, storyboards are often kept in black and white; the final video, however, must be in full color.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Use a 9:16 aspect ratio with a vertical orientation.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For the first-scene video, I’m now sending a link containing key images created from the ones you supplied. Please review them and leave your comments.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The review materials are available through this shared-folder link: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=sharing>

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: If you can, identify each suitable frame here by writing its name followed by "+". For any frame that needs changes, provide its name along with a comment specific to that frame.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The review notes were sent by email.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Resolution depends on the shot angle, and images taken from an angle this long cannot be improved beyond their current quality. Did you zoom in on the hero? Also, frames where the pulse moves do not always require many separate images, because the video already specifies how that should work.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Another revision of every image is what I’ll attempt next.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Using only photos of the characters and the location, we can create an alternative version of the video fragment without detailed photo frames. I’d like to show you that option as well.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: During 0-14 seconds, your video shows footage from a height, but the script does not include it. Should shots like that be added?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Because these set images are the ones you supplied, their current quality represents the maximum improvement possible from those sources.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I hadn’t realized this limitation existed. Do low-angle shots automatically have lower resolution, while higher-angle shots can achieve better resolution? I’m fine with changing the shot angles whenever doing so improves the quality of the set images.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Let’s secure all the other required material before spending time on the opening aerial establishing shot. I still want that shot, but it has a lower priority than everything else we need.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: My set images don’t seem high quality enough, and I hadn’t realized we would be limited to their existing resolution. Would generating new set images to use as starting frames improve the quality, and is that worth doing? I’m fine with that approach if it would help.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Despite being shown from a distant perspective, the hero is still marked in the image, even though his details are not visible.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: The possibility that you’ll want to add a voiceover later is why I asked for clarification. We should account for that now when timing the shots.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Could I create similar backgrounds? The image setup does affect the resulting quality.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Would medium and close-up angles work in place of the current distant shots?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: New sets are fine with me, provided they remain stylistically on point and consistent across the shots. If possible, though, I want to keep the long wide shots that open the sequence.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The framing moves from wide in the first set to mid in the second, then closer in the third.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Ok

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Sorry—the confusion came from my using "set" in more than one sense. There are three PAIRS of images, and each pair contains 1 shot of Kestrel and 1 shot of Red Fern. In framing order, the first two images are long/wide, the second two images are mid, and the third pair is closer, showing them from the waist up.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: To avoid doing the wrong job, can we review the details once more? I’ve already made the images a little better, but should we leave them like this with the background?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Would this long-angle approach for shot SQ4\_1 suit you? With this angle, the hero will usually not be in focus, while the frame remains on screen for a few seconds without zooming in.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Is this the angle for SQ4\_3?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Before I can rework the remaining shots, these revised ones need to be reconciled and reviewed. Some of the shots have already been reworked.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For review, I've shared the revised shots here: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: For this image set, I sent the review notes by email.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I've gone through the notes—thanks. The sets are actually distinct; still, could they be quite similar, and would that level of similarity be appropriate?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Although they may look similar, the resulting sets are still different; all I did was improve the images you supplied, not replace them.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Compared with my originals, these revised sets are much more similar to one another.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please review the materials in this shared folder: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=sharing>

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I've delivered the new images in this shared folder: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thanks—the latest images look much better now. I've sent my review notes separately by email.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Following your notes, I revised the image and included a few new frames in this delivery: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Because I'm only scaling the Kestrel set and changing nothing else, I honestly don't understand why you don't like it.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Would it help if I sent the background and the character without the background as separate assets, so you can show me your preferred arrangement?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I'm scaling the image in Photoshop.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: A perfect crop that retains the details you identified isn't possible with AI. I'll therefore do it manually, exactly as requested, using only Photoshop, and send you the result later.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Using Photoshop rather than AI, I completed the crop. You can review it here: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>. If it still isn't correct, I don't know another way to do it.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Overall, these look good, but a few small issues remain. The bridge behind Kestrel at his waste is badly placed; please remove it along with the bridge just above his head. To prevent the lower bridges from interfering, leave only the one upper bridge in the Kestrel images. The character shadows are also missing—can you restore them without changing anything else? Thanks for sticking with it!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: What kind of shadows do you mean? Could you describe them in more detail?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Do you need only the characters' shadows?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Have images 14a, 14b, 16a,16b,16c been reviewed as well?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: The character shadows visible in earlier renders are absent from these renders.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I’ll review the other images as well—sorry about that.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please review the folder here: <https://drive.riverstone.example/folders/synthetic-folder-riverstone-4826?usp=drive_link>. I’ve added new SQ4-SQ9, along with new shots that you haven’t commented on yet. Thanks.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: If possible, could you share all the requested changes together and in advance? Receiving adjustments piece by piece often means reworking everything from the beginning, which takes additional time. I’d really appreciate your understanding—thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I’m confused because I’ve been following your storyboard strictly, yet the SQ11 script says the angle changed. I’m supposed to be guided by the storyboard, right?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: For SQ12, has everything changed as well?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Additional work that wasn't initially anticipated can result when the script differs from the storyboard. To keep everything running smoothly, it would really help if the script matched the storyboard from the outset, or if any deviations were shared in advance. I just wanted to clarify that—thank you!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
I agree—you’re totally right, and I apologize. I should have highlighted those changes more directly and updated the storyboard reel.

There aren’t any other significant changes like that, but I’ll review the script and explicitly identify any remaining small tweaks so we are 100% clear on the direction.

Sorry again; I’ll circle back with that information.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Before I continue, should SQ5, SQ7 be changed? Also, can you confirm whether SQ10 onwards match the storyboard?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Please pause for now while I compile a list of any other changes before you do more work, so we don’t waste effort. Because I’m traveling today, I can only send it tomorrow or the day after.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: I want to identify each one specifically, even though only a few small tweaks remain.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Okay

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: While the other work is paused, you could keep going on SQ4 if you want, using my notes from yesterday about the energy blast.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: When it comes to SQ11 and SQ12, I no longer understand which frames should be included or how many are required.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Before work resumes, please allow me a day. During that time, I’ll capture any and all changes and write a detailed description of the remaining shots in SQ4.
